correctness.rationale: From Proposition 3.5 and Algorithm 3, the local scalar APG2 step has \(y=x+(z-x)/(1+|x-z|)\), \(z^+=2(1-a)y-x\) and \(x^+=(x+z^+)/2\). Its \(C^1\) derivative at zero is \(M_{1-a}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1-a\\-1&2(1-a)\end{pmatrix}\). The three-round derivative is \(T_s=M_sM_{4/5}^2\), with trace \((48s-32)/25\) and determinant \(16s/25\). Exact Jury factors are \((25-16s)/25\), \((57-32s)/25\), and \((64s-7)/25\), giving the sharp threshold. Below \(s=7/64\), the origin is a hyperbolic saddle, and the legal diagonal initialization is transverse to its stable eigenspace because the determinant of the initialized direction and its image is \((4s-12)/25\). The classical \(C^1\) local stable-manifold theorem then forces finite-time neighborhood exit for all sufficiently small nonzero legal starts. The state identity \(z_k=2x_k-x_{k-1}\) passes neighborhood exit to scalar optimization iterates. Above \(s=7/64\), strict Schur stability gives local exponential attraction. Ordinary proximal gradient has global three-step contraction factor \(16s/25\). All critical symbolic identities and the nonlinear derivative limit were checked with the standalone script; finite experiments are supplemental, not universal proofs.

value.rationale: For the same sequence of strongly convex objectives with no optimizer drift, the source acceleration develops a hyperbolic saddle below \(s=7/64\), yet ordinary proximal gradient remains globally contractive. The sharp numerical threshold and its verification under the genuine prescribed initialization create a useful method-specific robustness benchmark without generalizing to arbitrary momentum methods or claiming global divergence.
